title: Factory Method

solutions.title: One factory per job kind, looked up by kind, called from three thin wrappers
solutions.tradeoff: Adding a job kind is one new product class, one new factory subclass, and one registry entry - and zero edits to any of the three call sites. The price: a one-clause switch became four small files and an indirection a reader has to follow to see which class actually gets built for a given kind.

reviewFocus: Do counter.ts, reprint.ts and batch-import.ts still know about BusinessCardJob, BrochureJob or BannerJob by name, or only about createJob?
Is JOB_FACTORIES the only place a JobKind string is mapped to a class?
Does adding foil-stamping touch any of the three call-site files?
Is JobFactory doing real dispatch work, or would a plain Record<JobKind, (request) => PrintJob> of functions do the same job with one fewer layer?
